name: Online Social vs Non-Social Distraction — Attention fMRI
description: An OpenNeuro dataset (ds007126, ~14 GB) of 38 young adults performing a modified global-local attention task in the scanner under three distraction conditions: a social condition with a WeChat message icon and its sound alert, a non-social condition with a 360 browser download-complete icon and alert, and an undistracted baseline. Each condition ran as its own block of 48 event-related trials. Because the social and non-social interruptions are matched on timing and sensory form and differ only in social meaning, the dataset isolates what makes a social notification distinct as an attentional cue. Includes task fMRI, defaced T1 structural scans, trial-level accuracy and reaction times, MRIQC quality-control derivatives, and questionnaires on digital-media habits, affective traits, and attentional control in participants.tsv. Acquired at Sichuan Normal University on a 3T Siemens Prisma; the interleaved working-memory control runs are not part of the release.
citation: Liu C, Dai X, Yuan M, Kou J. (2026). An open fMRI dataset examining the effects of online social and non-social information distraction on attention. Scientific Data.
